post.description:
Create an echo record and return its representation.

Parameters
----------
payload : EchoRequest
    Request body containing the text to echo (and optional `source_url`).
response : fastapi.Response
    Raw HTTP response used to set headers (e.g., `Location`) for 201 Created.
service : EchoService
    Injected dependency from centralized accessors.

Returns
-------
EchoResponse
    Representation of the echoed text, including its character length.

Raises
------
ValueError
    Propagated if the underlying repository rejects invalid data (e.g., negative length).

Examples
--------
```python
>>> from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
>>> from your_service_name.backend.main import create_app
>>> client = TestClient(create_app())
>>> resp = client.post("/api/v1/echo", json={"text": "hello"})
>>> resp.status_code
201
>>> resp.headers["Location"].endswith("/api/v1/echo/history")
True
>>> resp.json()
{'text': 'hello', 'length': 5}
```

Notes
-----
- REST: 201 Created + `Location` header. For now, `Location` points to the collection
  (`/api/v1/echo/history`). If per-item identifiers are introduced later, update it to
  `/api/v1/echo/{id}`.

get.description:
Return previously stored echo entries.

Parameters
----------
service : EchoService
    Injected dependency; repository accessed via ``service.repo``.

Returns
-------
list[EchoResponse]
    History of echoed items.

Examples
--------
```python
>>> from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
>>> from your_service_name.backend.main import create_app
>>> client = TestClient(create_app())
>>> _ = client.post("/api/v1/echo", json={"text": "abc"})
>>> _ = client.post("/api/v1/echo", json={"text": "xyz"})
>>> resp = client.get("/api/v1/echo/history")
>>> resp.status_code
200
>>> resp.json()
[{'text': 'abc', 'length': 3}, {'text': 'xyz', 'length': 3}]
```

get.description:
Readiness probe.

Returns HTTP 200 ``{"status": "ok"}`` only when the database engine is
initialized AND a live ``SELECT 1`` succeeds. Returns HTTP 503
``{"status": "degraded"}`` otherwise.

The status code IS the contract: Kubernetes' readinessProbe keys off it, so
a pod whose DB tier is down is removed from the Service endpoints instead of
silently serving 5xx to clients — the failure mode this hardening closes
(see docs/E2E-FINDINGS.md §5.12). Because the probe also runs a live query,
a transient post-startup DB blip recovers on the next successful check
without a restart. Liveness is separate (/healthz) and must never depend on
the DB, so a database outage degrades readiness without restart-looping.

Return a bare health status for uptime/proxy monitors (e.g., a Kubernetes
liveness probe or the NGINX Ingress Controller health check).

Returns
-------
HealthStatus
    A payload containing `status="ok"`.

Notes
-----
- This endpoint is intentionally minimal for fast checks by load balancers.

delete.description:
Delete an item.

The single canonical soft-delete: sets ``deleted_at`` so the item drops out of
list/get. (There is no separate "archive" endpoint — delete *is* the soft-delete.)

Parameters
----------

    Item identifier.
_current_user : Principal
    Authenticated principal (gates writes; see backend.auth).
service : ItemService
    Injected dependency from centralized accessors.

Returns
-------
Response (204 No Content)

Raises
------
HTTPException 404
    If the item is not found.
